summary: On CelesTrak's 200 closest conjunctions, from the same element sets, our closest-approach distance differs by a median of 0.4 m and the time by less than a millisecond (CelesTrak publishes the distance to the nearest metre). CelesTrak's list was computed from orbit data about a day older than our latest run's. Of its close passes in our window, 31% of those where one object cannot manoeuvre are also in our run, against 9% for two working satellites of different fleets and 0% for two satellites of the same fleet: predictions for satellites that manoeuvre do not survive a day of new data.
